messages:
margot: Heads-up — Acme reporting repeated 429s on /v1/embeddings around 00:12 PST, lasted ~15m. They pasted this header from their client: `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `retry-after: 2`. Can someone triage?

eng-oncall-bot: Alert fired: tenant:acme || rule:tenant_rate_limit_429s || 00:12-00:27 UTC. Link: https://console.redwood/d/alerts/tenant-rate-limit-429s

jon: I'm pulling request_events for tenant=acme now. quick preview shows a spike: ~1.1k 429s/min at 00:13. Likely a burst + retries.

jon: SQL I ran: ```sql
SELECT minute, count(*) as errs
FROM request_events
WHERE tenant_id='acme' AND status=429
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

priya: Do we know which model/route variant? Was that embeddings-prod or a fallback?

jon: Route = /v1/embeddings, model_id=rdx-embed-1:v2. k=v_host shows prod. No fallback.

kevin: Acme is on Startup plan — baseline rate 50k/min with 2x burst window (100k) for 5m. If they retried in parallel it could blow the burst. Can we confirm token bucket consumption?

jon: Token bucket meters show a short window where `burst_capacity` went to 0. Snippet from telemetry: ```
metric: tenant_burst_capacity{tenant='acme'}
00:11: 48000
00:12: 8000
00:13: 0
00:14: 0
00:15: 32000 (recovering)
```

tara: Dashboard: https://console.redwood/d/l/limits/tenant-acme shows per-route breakdown and model attribution. I see the 00:12 spike originated from route /v1/embeddings > model rdx-embed-1:v2 > region us-west-2.

datadog-bot: Graph: RateLimitExceeded count, 00:12-00:16 UTC; sample request IDs: req_9a8, req_9b0, req_9b7.

margot: Customer says they had a nightly batch that started 00:10 and retried on 429 with exponential backoff but retry multiplier was low (1s). They admit parallelism=200.

priya: That matches retry storm pattern. For attribution: we need to show them per-minute QPS by route and by client API key. Can we export the 429s grouped by api_key?

jon: Yep. Ran: ```sql
SELECT api_key, count(*) FROM request_events
WHERE tenant_id='acme' AND status=429 AND minute >= '2026-03-17 00:10'
GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20;
``` Result: single api_key `sk-live-ACMEx` accounts for 98% of 429s.

kevin: So ownership: customer app (api_key) caused it. For support reply we should: 1) point to dashboard 2) give repro steps 3) suggest short-term config (increase burst cap or throttle client)

margot: I'll draft reply. For repro steps — can we provide a minimal script they can run that demonstrates the failure?

jon: Minimal repro (bash): ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACMEx" -d '{"input":"test"}' &
done; wait
```

priya: Also include a way to inspect `x-rate-limit-*` headers from one request: `curl -I ...` so they can see remaining tokens.

margot: Proposed short-term mitigations in response to customer: - temporarily raise tenant burst cap to 150k for 30m (if they ask) - advise to reduce parallelism and implement jittered backoff - provide their per-api_key 429 attribution export

kevin: I can approve a temporary bump. Ticket opened: #SR-4821. I'll note expiration + rollback.

margot: I've exported CSV of the api_key breakdown and attached to the support ticket. Draft reply to customer: "We saw a short-lived burst from your API key X that exhausted your burst capacity; please reduce parallelism and add jittered backoff. We can temporarily raise your burst cap while you remediate."

jon: Engineering note for runtime team: observed unusual pattern — 200 parallel small embedding calls per client; suggest we add a sampled per-tenant heatmap to limits dashboard and an alert for sustained token_bucket=0 > 2m. Filing runtime issue.

priya: For observability follow-up: create an A/B dashboard tile that shows (1) per-tenant token bucket, (2) per-route 429 rate, (3) top api_keys during window. That will make triage faster.

margot: Action items: [x] export attribution CSV, [x] reply to customer, [ ] eng-runtime issue (#E-1147) for auto-alert, [x] temporary burst bump ticket (#SR-4821). I'll close once runtime confirms alerting work. Thanks team :thumbsup:
